text: 1. Short title and extent.—This Act may be called the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. It extends to the whole of India and it applies also to all citizens of India outside India.
section_title: Short title and extent

text: 2. Definitions.—In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires: 'public duty' means a duty in the discharge of which the State, the public or the community at large has an interest. 'public servant' includes any person in the service or pay of the Government, any person in the service or pay of a local authority, any Judge, any arbitrator, any person authorised to perform a public duty, and office-bearers of government-aided institutions, among others. 'undue advantage' means any gratification whatever, other than legal remuneration; the word 'gratification' is not limited to pecuniary gratifications or to gratifications estimable in money.
section_title: Definitions

text: 3. Power to appoint special Judges.—The Central Government or the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint special Judges to try offences punishable under this Act, and any conspiracy, attempt, or abetment of such offences. A person is not qualified for appointment as a special Judge unless he is or has been a Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge, or Assistant Sessions Judge.
section_title: Power to appoint special Judges

text: 4. Cases triable by special Judges.—Offences under this Act shall be tried only by special Judges. The trial of an offence shall be held, as far as practicable, on a day-to-day basis, with an endeavour to conclude the trial within two years, extendable for recorded reasons up to a maximum of four years in aggregate.
section_title: Cases triable by special Judges

text: 5. Procedure and powers of special Judge.—A special Judge may take cognizance of offences without the accused being committed for trial, and shall follow the procedure prescribed for the trial of warrant cases by Magistrates. A special Judge may tender a pardon to a person with a view to obtaining evidence of an offence under this Act.
section_title: Procedure and powers of special Judge

text: 6. Power to try summarily.—Where a special Judge tries certain offences relating to contravention of orders under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, the special Judge shall try the offence in a summary way, subject to specified sentencing limits and appeal rights.
section_title: Power to try summarily

text: 7. Offence relating to public servant being bribed.—Any public servant who (a) obtains or accepts or attempts to obtain from any person an undue advantage, with the intention to perform or cause performance of a public duty improperly or dishonestly, or to forbear or cause forbearance to perform such duty, either by himself or by another public servant; or (b) obtains or accepts or attempts to obtain an undue advantage from any person as a reward for the improper or dishonest performance of a public duty, or for forbearing to perform such duty; or (c) performs or induces another public servant to perform improperly or dishonestly a public duty, or to forbear performance of such duty, in anticipation of or in consequence of accepting an undue advantage from any person, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation 1: The obtaining, accepting, or attempting to obtain an undue advantage shall itself constitute an offence even if the performance of the public duty is not or has not been improper. Illustration: A public servant 'S' asks a person 'P' to give him an amount of five thousand rupees to process his routine ration card application on time. 'S' is guilty of an offence under this section.
section_title: Offence relating to public servant being bribed

text: 7A. Taking undue advantage to influence public servant by corrupt or illegal means or by exercise of personal influence.—Whoever accepts or obtains or attempts to obtain from another person, for himself or for any other person, any undue advantage as a motive or reward to induce a public servant, by corrupt or illegal means or by exercise of personal influence, to perform or cause performance of a public duty improperly or dishonestly, or to forbear or cause to forbear such public duty, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
section_title: Taking undue advantage to influence public servant by corrupt or illegal means or by exercise of personal influence

text: 8. Offence relating to bribing of a public servant.—Any person who gives or promises to give an undue advantage to another person, with intention to induce a public servant to perform improperly a public duty, or to reward such public servant for the improper performance of a public duty, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both. This section shall not apply where a person is compelled to give such undue advantage, provided the person so compelled reports the matter to the law enforcement authority or investigating agency within seven days from the date of giving such undue advantage. Illustration: A person 'P' gives a public servant 'S' an amount of ten thousand rupees to ensure that he is granted a license over all other bidders. 'P' is guilty of an offence under this sub-section.
section_title: Offence relating to bribing of a public servant

text: 9. Offence relating to bribing a public servant by a commercial organisation.—Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a commercial organisation, such organisation shall be punishable with fine, if any person associated with such commercial organisation gives or promises to give any undue advantage to a public servant intending to obtain or retain business, or an advantage in the conduct of business, for such commercial organisation. It is a defence for the organisation to prove it had adequate procedures in place to prevent such conduct.
section_title: Offence relating to bribing a public servant by a commercial organisation

text: 10. Person in charge of commercial organisation to be guilty of offence.—Where an offence under section 9 is committed by a commercial organisation with the consent or connivance of any director, manager, secretary or other officer, such person shall be guilty of the offence and punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
section_title: Person in charge of commercial organisation to be guilty of offence

text: 11. Public servant obtaining undue advantage, without consideration from person concerned in proceeding or business transacted by such public servant.—Whoever, being a public servant, accepts or obtains or attempts to obtain, for himself or for any other person, any undue advantage without consideration, or for a consideration he knows to be inadequate, from any person he knows to be concerned in any proceeding or business transacted by such public servant, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall be not less than six months but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
section_title: Public servant obtaining undue advantage, without consideration from person concerned in proceeding or business transacted by such public servant

text: 12. Punishment for abetment of offences.—Whoever abets any offence punishable under this Act, whether or not that offence is committed in consequence of that abetment, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years, but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
section_title: Punishment for abetment of offences

text: 13. Criminal misconduct by a public servant.—A public servant is said to commit the offence of criminal misconduct if he dishonestly or fraudulently misappropriates or otherwise converts for his own use any property entrusted to him or under his control as a public servant, or if he intentionally enriches himself illicitly during the period of his office. A person is presumed to have intentionally enriched himself illicitly if he, or someone on his behalf, is found in possession of pecuniary resources or property disproportionate to his known sources of income which he cannot satisfactorily account for. Punishment: imprisonment for a term which shall be not less than four years but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
section_title: Criminal misconduct by a public servant

text: 14. Punishment for habitual offender.—Whoever, convicted of an offence under this Act, subsequently commits an offence punishable under this Act, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
section_title: Punishment for habitual offender

text: 15. Punishment for attempt.—Whoever attempts to commit an offence referred to in clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 13 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than two years but which may extend to five years, and with fine.
section_title: Punishment for attempt

text: 16. Matters to be taken into consideration for fixing fine.—Where a sentence of fine is imposed under sections 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13(2), 14 or 15, the court shall take into consideration the amount or value of the property the accused obtained by committing the offence, or the disproportionate pecuniary resources or property referred to in section 13, in fixing the amount of the fine.
section_title: Matters to be taken into consideration for fixing fine

text: 17. Persons authorised to investigate.—No police officer below the rank of Inspector of Police (Delhi Special Police Establishment), Assistant Commissioner of Police (metropolitan areas), or Deputy Superintendent of Police (elsewhere) shall investigate any offence punishable under this Act, or make any arrest, without the order of a Metropolitan Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class, except where authorised by the State Government by general or special order.
chapter_title: Investigation Into Cases Under The Act
section_title: Persons authorised to investigate

text: 17A. Enquiry or Inquiry or investigation of offences relatable to recommendations made or decision taken by public servant in discharge of official functions or duties.—No police officer shall conduct any enquiry, inquiry or investigation into any offence alleged to have been committed by a public servant under this Act, where the alleged offence relates to any recommendation made or decision taken by such public servant in discharge of official functions or duties, without previous approval of the competent government or authority — except for cases involving arrest of a person on the spot on the charge of accepting or attempting to accept any undue advantage.
chapter_title: Investigation Into Cases Under The Act
section_title: Enquiry or Inquiry or investigation of offences relatable to recommendations made or decision taken by public servant in discharge of official functions or duties

text: 18. Power to inspect bankers' books.—A police officer investigating an offence under this Act, not below the rank of Superintendent of Police (or specially authorised), may inspect bankers' books relating to the accounts of persons suspected of committing the offence, and the bank concerned shall be bound to assist the police officer.
chapter_title: Investigation Into Cases Under The Act
section_title: Power to inspect bankers' books

text: 18A. Provisions of Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1944 to apply to attachment under this Act.—The provisions of the Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1944 apply, as far as may be, to the attachment, administration, and execution of orders of attachment or confiscation of money or property procured by means of an offence under this Act, subject to certain modifications.
section_title: Provisions of Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1944 to apply to attachment under this Act

text: 19. Previous sanction necessary for prosecution.—No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under sections 7, 11, 13 and 15 alleged to have been committed by a public servant, except with the previous sanction of the competent Government or authority. A private complainant must first file a complaint in a competent court, and the court must not have dismissed it, before requesting sanction. The competent authority must provide the public servant an opportunity to be heard, and should convey its decision within three months, extendable by one month for legal consultation.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Previous sanction necessary for prosecution

text: 20. Presumption where public servant accepts any undue advantage.—Where, in a trial of an offence punishable under section 7 or section 11, it is proved that a public servant has accepted, obtained, or attempted to obtain any undue advantage from any person, it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that he did so as a motive or reward under section 7 or without adequate consideration under section 11.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Presumption where public servant accepts any undue advantage

text: 21. Accused person to be a competent witness.—Any person charged with an offence punishable under this Act shall be a competent witness for the defence and may give evidence on oath, subject to conditions including that he shall not be called as a witness except at his own request.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Accused person to be a competent witness

text: 22. The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 to apply subject to certain modifications.—The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 applies to proceedings under this Act subject to specified modifications regarding witness lists, adjournment of proceedings, and trial in the absence of the accused.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 to apply subject to certain modifications

text: 23. Particulars in a charge in relation to an offence under section 13(1)(a).—Where an accused is charged with an offence under clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 13, it is sufficient to describe the property concerned and the dates between which the offence is alleged to have been committed, without specifying exact items or dates, provided the period does not exceed one year.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Particulars in a charge in relation to an offence under section 13(1)(a)

text: 25. Military, Naval and Air Force or other law not to be affected.—Nothing in this Act affects the jurisdiction or procedure applicable under the Army Act 1950, Air Force Act 1950, Navy Act 1957, Border Security Force Act 1968, Coast Guard Act 1978, and National Security Guard Act 1986. The court of a special Judge is deemed a court of ordinary criminal justice for the purposes of those laws.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Military, Naval and Air Force or other law not to be affected

text: 26. Special Judges appointed under Act 46 of 1952 to be special Judges appointed under this Act.—Every special Judge appointed under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1952 and holding office on the commencement of this Act is deemed a special Judge appointed under section 3 of this Act, and continues to deal with pending proceedings accordingly.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Special Judges appointed under Act 46 of 1952 to be special Judges appointed under this Act

text: 27. Appeal and revision.—The High Court may exercise all powers of appeal and revision conferred by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 on a High Court, as if the court of the special Judge were a Court of Session.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Appeal and revision

text: 28. Act to be in addition to any other law.—The provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law in force, and nothing in this Act exempts any public servant from any other proceeding that might be instituted against him.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Act to be in addition to any other law

text: 29A. Power to make rules.—The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act, including guidelines for commercial organisations under section 9 and for sanction of prosecution under section 19.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Power to make rules

text: 30. Repeal and saving.—The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1952 are repealed. Anything done or action taken under the repealed Acts is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provision of this Act, so far as it is not inconsistent with this Act.
chapter_title: Sanction for Prosecution and Other Miscellaneous Provisions
section_title: Repeal and saving
